title: Six Slippery Snails
subtitle: Clusters SN & SL
description: This exercise targets the SN and SL consonant clusters, training smooth and simultaneous articulation of S followed immediately by a nasal or liquid consonant. These clusters are a common stumbling block at speed.
tip: Don't insert a vowel between the S and the following consonant — 'snail' is one syllable, not 'suh-nail'. Get the S and N touching in the same breath before the vowel begins.
phrases: Six slippery snails slid slowly seaward.
Six slippery snails slid silently along six slick slabs.
Slippery slimey snakes slunk slowly sideways.
The sleek snow sled slid down the snowy slope.
Sneezing snails leave slimy snail trails on slick glass.
Slim sly snakes slithered past sleeping snails on slippery stones.
